evidence_chain: Fact: FormFactor reported Q1 2026 revenue of $226.1 million, up 32.0% year over year, and said it delivered record DRAM revenue with increased demand in HBM applications. Source: FormFactor Q1 2026 earnings release, https://investors.formfactor.com/static-files/7f524069-6dfe-466b-9cbe-9548f985ab73

Fact: Q1 2026 DRAM revenue was $82.9 million versus $48.9 million in Q1 2025; Probe Cards Segment revenue was $198.2 million versus $136.6 million in Q1 2025. Source: FormFactor Q1 2026 supplemental information, https://investors.formfactor.com/static-files/599ca1f9-f7ee-4701-b044-ec37752aba20

Fact: Q1 2026 non-GAAP gross margin was 49.0%, up from 43.9% in Q4 2025 and 39.2% in Q1 2025; FormFactor guided Q2 2026 revenue to $240 million plus/minus $5 million and non-GAAP gross margin to 49.5% plus/minus 1.5%. Source: FormFactor Q1 2026 earnings release, https://investors.formfactor.com/static-files/7f524069-6dfe-466b-9cbe-9548f985ab73

Fact: Q1 2026 customer concentration showed SK hynix at 29.5% of revenue and NVIDIA at 10.2%; Samsung was below 10%. Source: FormFactor Q1 2026 supplemental information, https://investors.formfactor.com/static-files/599ca1f9-f7ee-4701-b044-ec37752aba20

Fact: FormFactor’s 2025 10-K says fiscal 2025 record revenue was led by strong growth in DRAM, particularly demand for HBM chips used in generative AI applications. Source: FormFactor FY2025 Form 10-K, https://investors.formfactor.com/static-files/f903ad72-0783-4e11-bdcc-cfae526f1f96

Fact: FormFactor’s 2025 10-K disclosed SK hynix represented 22.9% of FY2025 revenue and 18.9% of FY2024 revenue; it also disclosed quarterly SK hynix concentration ranging from 19.2% to 25.0% during FY2025. Source: FormFactor FY2025 Form 10-K, https://investors.formfactor.com/static-files/f903ad72-0783-4e11-bdcc-cfae526f1f96

Fact: FormFactor says its HFTAP K32 probe card enables wafer-level speed testing up to 3.2 GHz / 6.4 Gbps for next-generation known-good-die memory and supports products including HBM3, DDR5, LPDDR5, GDDR5 and GDDR6. Source: FormFactor HFTAP product page, https://www.formfactor.com/product/probe-cards/dram/hftap-series/

Fact: FormFactor’s HFTAP product page explicitly connects KGD testing to avoiding scrap in final stacked/assembled packages and says its advanced MEMS probe card architecture can verify devices used in the HBM stack, including fine-pitch interposers. Source: FormFactor HFTAP product page, https://www.formfactor.com/product/probe-cards/dram/hftap-series/

Fact: FormFactor’s 2025 10-K states it purchased a Farmers Branch, Texas manufacturing site in June 2025 with 50,000 square feet of existing cleanroom space, expected to begin ramping production in late fiscal 2026. Source: FormFactor FY2025 Form 10-K, https://investors.formfactor.com/static-files/f903ad72-0783-4e11-bdcc-cfae526f1f96
Fact: As of June 8, 2026, FORM market cap was approximately $9.72 billion, placing it near the upper end of the preferred underfollowed mid-cap range. Source: web finance quote, ticker FORM.

Inference: The combination of record DRAM revenue, SK hynix concentration, HBM-specific product language, and margin improvement is consistent with an HBM probe-card mix shift, but company disclosures do not yet provide enough granularity to prove exact HBM revenue or durable supply tightness.

Hypothesis: If HBM4 and next-generation DDR/HBM test requirements raise probe-card complexity and qualification barriers, FORM’s installed customer relationships and advanced MEMS/probe-card technology could become a recurring pre-packaging bottleneck.
falsification_plan: Falsify if future 10-Qs or earnings calls show DRAM revenue growth slowing sharply while HBM capacity additions continue, implying FORM is not capturing the HBM test ramp.
Falsify if management stops referring to HBM as a growth driver or refuses to confirm repeat demand beyond a single customer/product generation.
Falsify if SK hynix remains the only obvious memory-related >10% customer and Samsung/Micron-related signals do not appear in geographic, customer, or commentary data.
Falsify if non-GAAP probe-card margins fail to remain near or above the Q1 2026 level despite higher DRAM/HBM mix.
Falsify if customer lead times normalize quickly, backlog/order commentary weakens, or the Farmers Branch capacity ramp creates excess capacity rather than relieving constrained demand.
Falsify if competitors announce major HBM probe-card wins at leading memory makers or if memory customers publicly discuss broader dual-sourcing away from FORM.
Falsify if HBM makers reduce wafer-level test intensity or shift yield-learning economics toward later-stage package test, lowering the importance of pre-packaging probe cards.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether HBM-related probe-card demand is recurring, supply-constrained, margin-accretive, and diversified across more than one HBM supplier, rather than a temporary SK hynix-heavy ramp or one product-generation win.
next_research_tasks: Pull FormFactor Q2 2026 results after the quarter ending June 27, 2026 and compare actual DRAM revenue, probe-card margin, customer concentration, and Q3 guidance against the Q1 2026 baseline.

Search FormFactor investor-day and conference transcripts for exact language on SmartMatrix adoption, second HBM customer ramps, HBM4, DDR5, lead times, backlog, and Farmers Branch capacity allocation.
Cross-check SK hynix, Samsung, and Micron HBM capacity-expansion plans against FORM’s Korea/Taiwan/US geographic revenue mix to test whether FORM revenue moves with actual HBM wafer capacity.
Look for procurement, qualification, patent, and technical-paper evidence linking FORM probe cards to HBM3E/HBM4 testing at multiple memory makers.
Compare FORM against direct and indirect probe-card competitors to assess whether high-frequency HBM probe cards have scarce supplier characteristics or normal multi-vendor competition.

Build a quarterly tracker with DRAM revenue, Probe Cards Segment revenue, Probe Cards Segment GAAP gross margin, non-GAAP gross margin, SK hynix percentage, Samsung/Micron indicators, NVIDIA/AI logic customer concentration, capex, inventory, deferred revenue, and free cash flow.

Interview or source industry checks from memory test engineers or ATE/probe-card supply-chain participants to verify lead times, qualification cycles, replacement risk, and whether HBM probe cards are genuinely supply constrained.
risks: Customer concentration risk: SK hynix was 29.5% of Q1 2026 revenue and 22.9% of FY2025 revenue; this creates risk that the HBM signal is one-customer-heavy rather than broad-based.

Disclosure risk: FORM does not yet provide a clean HBM revenue line, HBM gross margin, probe-card backlog, or lead-time data, making the thesis partly dependent on inference from DRAM revenue and customer mix.
Cyclicality risk: semiconductor test and probe-card demand can fall quickly if memory capex slows, HBM supply overshoots, or customers digest inventory.
Competitive risk: memory makers could qualify alternative probe-card vendors, use different test strategies, reduce test content, or internalize/dual-source critical probe-card technologies.

Margin-quality risk: Q1 2026 GAAP gross margin was affected by restructuring charges, while non-GAAP margin improvement may include operational changes, tariff effects, mix, or timing; margin-accretion specifically from HBM is not isolated.
Capacity execution risk: Farmers Branch ramp, manufacturing consolidation, and cleanroom expansion may create start-up costs or delays before they improve supply capacity.

Valuation/attention risk: with a roughly $9.7 billion market cap and strong recent results, some HBM upside may already be reflected; this report is research prioritization only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
Technology-generation risk: HBM4/HBM4E probe-card requirements may differ from HBM3/HBM3E, and a strong position in one generation may not automatically transfer to the next.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: AI infrastructure demand -> GPUs/ASICs and accelerator modules -> HBM capacity expansion by memory makers -> HBM wafer sort / known-good-die testing -> high-frequency DRAM/HBM probe cards and ATE interface -> advanced packaging with logic die/interposer/HBM stack -> AI accelerator system integration -> data-center deployment. FORM sits at the pre-packaging wafer-level electrical test node, upstream of advanced packaging and downstream of HBM wafer fabrication.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 假设：AI 服务器和加速器对 HBM 的需求上升，使 HBM/高端 DRAM 在进入 2.5D/3D 先进封装和昂贵系统集成前，需要更多、更高频、更可靠的晶圆级测试与 known-good-die 验证。FormFactor 如果在 HBM/DRAM 探针卡上拥有可重复订单、多客户导入、供给受限和利润率改善，那么它可能不是普通半导体测试周期股，而是 AI 内存扩产链条中一个偏上游、较窄、被行业分类掩盖的测试卡点。当前证据已支持“HBM 正在显著拉动 DRAM probe card 收入”这一事实，但“FormFactor 是不可绕开的瓶颈供应商”仍是待验证假设。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Hypothesis: rising AI accelerator and server demand increases the need for HBM and high-end DRAM wafer-level testing before expensive 2.5D/3D advanced packaging and system integration. If FormFactor’s HBM/DRAM probe-card business proves recurring, diversified across memory customers, supply-constrained, and margin-accretive, FORM may deserve to be studied as a narrow AI memory expansion supplier rather than a generic cyclical semiconductor test name. Current evidence supports the fact that HBM is materially driving DRAM probe-card momentum, but the stronger claim that FORM is an unavoidable chokepoint remains unproven.
deep_reports.title_cn: FormFactor：AI HBM 扩产链条里的晶圆级探针卡窄口假设
deep_reports.title_en: FormFactor: Wafer-Level Probe Cards as a Potential HBM Test Chokepoint in AI Infrastructure
deep_reports.why_underfollowed: FORM is usually screened as a semiconductor test/probe-card company rather than as an AI infrastructure supplier. The AI linkage is one or two supply-chain steps away from the obvious GPU and data-center capex narrative: the signal appears inside HBM yield, KGD validation, probe-card complexity, memory-customer qualification, and advanced-packaging pre-test rather than in direct AI accelerator sales.

evidence_chain: [Cached brief | claim_type: inference] Vertiv is identified as the reference leader for AI data-center power and thermal infrastructure, with chokepoint logic tied to higher AI rack power density and rising demand for power distribution, UPS, thermal management, liquid cooling, and facility infrastructure.

[External context 2 | fact from provided search context] A June 4, 2026 Tiger Daily Alpha note frames the AI bottleneck as shifting toward megawatts and memory, and names Vertiv as a primary power-and-cooling exposure with a reported backlog figure and rack-level power/thermal interface framing. Source: https://princetonchen.substack.com/p/tiger-daily-alpha-jun-4-the-bottleneck

[External context 4 | fact from provided search context] Atlas Peak Research’s April 30, 2026 mega-cap AI earnings review describes AI infrastructure bottlenecks as broader than GPUs, spanning accelerators, ASICs, CPUs, HBM/DRAM, networking, power, cooling, and data-center deployment. Source: https://www.atlaspeakresearch.com/report/74645c

[External context 1 | fact from provided search context] Johnson Lee’s June 6, 2026 Serenity methodology article describes the broader bottleneck-hunting approach: start with AI demand, then identify physical supply-chain constraints such as upstream photonics, power, and infrastructure bottlenecks rather than only obvious GPU beneficiaries. Source: https://johnsonlee.io/2026/06/06/serenity-methodology-cannot-be-skill.en/

[Methodology context | fact from cached Serenity skill digest] Serenity-style research starts from a broad theme, decomposes the supply chain, looks for low supplier count, long qualification cycles, expansion difficulty, customer certification, and hard-to-substitute bottlenecks, then maps them back to public companies and falsification tests.
[Inference] Vertiv’s benchmark value comes from being close to the AI rack/facility deployment constraint, but its high attention level makes market-pricing checks essential.

[Hypothesis to verify] If Vertiv can disclose or demonstrate sustained AI/data-center order growth, liquid-cooling adoption, backlog conversion, and margin durability, it remains a strong benchmark for the power/cooling chokepoint; if those signals weaken, the broader power/cooling thesis may need to be narrowed to different nodes.
falsification_plan: Falsify or downgrade if backlog growth slows materially, backlog duration shortens for the wrong reasons, cancellations rise, or management indicates weaker order momentum in AI/data-center verticals.
Falsify or downgrade if AI-specific demand cannot be supported separately and appears indistinguishable from a normal data-center or critical-infrastructure cycle.
Falsify or downgrade if liquid-cooling revenue remains immaterial, customer qualifications are delayed, or deployments remain pilot-level rather than production-level.
Falsify or downgrade if gross or operating margins compress due to competition, cost inflation, capacity additions, unfavorable mix, or service execution issues.
Falsify or downgrade if cash conversion deteriorates despite revenue growth, suggesting working-capital strain or low-quality backlog conversion.
Falsify or downgrade if market valuation embeds backlog conversion, liquid-cooling penetration, and margin expansion assumptions that exceed realistic delivery capacity.

Falsify or downgrade the broader power/cooling chokepoint if hyperscaler capex shifts away from power-dense deployments, rack-density growth slows, or grid/interconnection delays become the dominant bottleneck outside Vertiv’s monetizable scope.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether AI-specific backlog, data-center order conversion, liquid-cooling adoption, and margin expansion continue strongly enough to justify expectations already embedded in the stock. The key signal is not generic data-center exposure; it is the conversion of AI-driven power/cooling demand into durable revenue, operating margin, cash flow, and customer-qualified product adoption.
next_research_tasks: Pull Vertiv’s latest 10-K, 10-Q, earnings call transcripts, and investor presentations; extract data-center/AI order commentary, backlog, book-to-bill, organic growth, segment margins, and cash conversion.

Build a quarterly KPI table: orders, backlog, book-to-bill, revenue growth, Americas vs international mix, data-center mix, gross margin, operating margin, free cash flow, and inventory/working-capital intensity.

Search for specific liquid-cooling disclosures: product lines, customer qualifications, capacity additions, revenue contribution, partnerships, and whether deployments are pilot, ramp, or scaled production.

Compare Vertiv against reference peers and adjacent suppliers: Eaton, Schneider Electric, GE Vernova, nVent, Modine, Quanta Services, Comfort Systems, and niche thermal/electrical component companies.

Run a market-pricing check: compare current enterprise value, forward revenue/EBITDA/earnings multiples, consensus growth, backlog duration, and margin expectations versus historical ranges and peers.

Identify underfollowed second-order candidates that benchmark favorably against Vertiv: liquid-cooling components, heat exchangers, CDU suppliers, power modules, switchgear components, test/certification providers, commissioning services, and data-center electrical contractors.

Verify customer concentration and qualification cycles: determine whether Vertiv is tied to specific hyperscalers, colocation providers, OEMs, or integrators, and whether design wins are sticky or rebid frequently.

Create an upgrade/downgrade evidence ladder: upgrade only with primary-source proof of AI-specific order growth, material liquid-cooling revenue, durable margin bridge, and strong cash conversion; downgrade with weak attribution, margin compression, or excessive valuation assumptions.
risks: Valuation risk: as a high-attention AI infrastructure beneficiary, Vertiv may already price in aggressive backlog conversion, sustained margin expansion, and rapid liquid-cooling adoption.
Backlog quality risk: headline backlog may include non-AI, lower-margin, delayed, or cancellable orders; backlog duration and conversion timing matter more than the absolute figure.
AI attribution risk: data-center growth may be difficult to separate from normal critical infrastructure, colocation, enterprise, telecom, and replacement-cycle demand.
Liquid-cooling adoption risk: market expectations may run ahead of actual revenue contribution, customer qualification timelines, service complexity, or deployment readiness.
Margin normalization risk: current margins could be helped by mix, pricing, supply tightness, or operating leverage that may fade as competitors add capacity.
Competitive risk: electrical equipment, thermal management, and liquid-cooling markets include large diversified competitors and specialized suppliers that may pressure pricing or win key designs.
Execution risk: rapid AI data-center deployment requires supply-chain coordination across power modules, cooling systems, installation, services, and customer-specific engineering.
Macro and capex risk: hyperscaler or colocation capex digestion, grid delays, financing pressure, or energy constraints could delay revenue recognition even if long-term demand remains intact.

Evidence risk: the current report relies on cached brief and external search snippets; primary filings, earnings transcripts, investor presentations, and segment disclosures still need to be checked before promoting any claim to high-confidence fact.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: AI infrastructure supply chain map: downstream demand comes from hyperscaler and enterprise AI data-center capacity expansion; system layer includes AI servers, racks, clusters, networking, and deployment facilities; Vertiv maps to the facility/rack infrastructure layer, including critical power, power distribution, UPS, thermal management, liquid cooling, and related services. It is downstream of GPUs/ASICs/HBM/networking but upstream or parallel to actual data-center energization and deployment. In Serenity terms, Vertiv is a reference leader for the megawatt/rack-density chokepoint, useful for comparing more obscure suppliers such as component vendors, thermal modules, electrical equipment firms, grid contractors, test/certification providers, and niche cooling suppliers.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 【推论】AI 机柜功率密度上升，使供配电、UPS、热管理、液冷和机房基础设施从“配套环节”变成部署约束。Vertiv 位于机柜级与机房级电力/散热交界处，因此可作为 AI 数据中心电力与热管理瓶颈的参考标杆。研究重点不是证明 Vertiv 是否有 AI 暴露，而是验证 backlog 是否能顺利转收入、液冷采用是否真实放量、利润率扩张是否可持续，以及市场估值是否已经提前反映了这些好消息。
deep_reports.thesis_en: [Inference] Rising AI rack density is turning power distribution, UPS, thermal management, liquid cooling, and facility infrastructure from supporting layers into deployment constraints. Vertiv sits near the rack/facility power-and-thermal interface, making it a reference benchmark for the AI data-center power and cooling chokepoint. The research question is not whether Vertiv has AI exposure; it is whether backlog converts into revenue, liquid-cooling adoption becomes material, margins remain durable, and valuation already discounts most of the bottleneck value.
deep_reports.title_cn: Vertiv：AI 数据中心电力与散热卡点的参考标杆，而非冷门发现标的
deep_reports.title_en: Vertiv: Reference Leader for AI Data-Center Power and Thermal Chokepoints, Not an Underfollowed Discovery
deep_reports.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed. Vertiv is a high-attention reference leader. Its role in this funnel is to prevent the research process from mistaking obvious exposure for hidden alpha. The company provides benchmark metrics for backlog, order growth, book-to-bill, AI data-center mix, liquid-cooling adoption, margin expansion, and market-pricing risk. Smaller or less obvious companies should be compared against Vertiv’s evidence quality and valuation expectations rather than treated as attractive merely because they mention AI data centers.

evidence_chain: Fact: On September 16, 2025, Cohu announced additional orders for its Neon platform from a leading U.S.-based memory and data-storage customer for inspection and metrology of HBM devices used in HPC and generative AI applications. Source: https://ir.cohu.com/news-releases/news-release-details/cohu-secures-additional-neon-orders-raises-2025-forecasted-hbm

Fact: In the same September 16, 2025 release, Cohu said it had shipped its first system configured for HBM4 inspection and raised 2025 forecasted HBM revenue to $10-11 million. Source: https://ir.cohu.com/news-releases/news-release-details/cohu-secures-additional-neon-orders-raises-2025-forecasted-hbm

Fact: Cohu’s Q1 2026 release reported net sales of $125.1 million, approximately 60% recurring, gross margin of 46.3%, and Q2 2026 sales guidance of $144 million +/- $7 million. Source: https://ir.cohu.com/news-releases/news-release-details/cohu-reports-first-quarter-2026-results

Fact: In Q1 2026, Cohu stated it was increasing its AI-driven compute addressable market estimate to approximately $750 million and raising FY26 high-performance computing revenue outlook to approximately $80-100 million. Source: https://ir.cohu.com/news-releases/news-release-details/cohu-reports-first-quarter-2026-results

Fact: Cohu’s FY2025 Form 10-K describes the company as a supplier of semiconductor test automation and interface solutions, and a growing provider of test equipment, inspection and metrology solutions, and software analytics to optimize semiconductor manufacturing yield and productivity. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/21535/000143774926004339/cohu20251227_10k.htm

Fact: Cohu’s FY2025 Form 10-K says the company is capitalizing on high-growth opportunities including HBM inspection, high-performance processor test in AI applications, wide-bandgap test, and AI-driven software analytics. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/21535/000143774926004339/cohu20251227_10k.htm
Fact: As of June 8, 2026 17:19:32 UTC, web finance data showed COHU market capitalization around $2.50 billion, placing it in the mid-cap bucket. Source: web finance quote in this run.

Inference: HBM and advanced-packaging manufacturing likely create more inspection/metrology burden because dense stacks, micro-pillars, package interfaces, and production yield windows make defects more expensive and harder to tolerate.

Hypothesis: COHU’s Neon and related inspection/metrology/test platforms could become a narrow quality-control gate if memory or packaging customers standardize on them for repeat HBM production workflows.

Evidence gap: Current public evidence supports HBM traction but does not yet prove broad customer adoption, material revenue mix transformation, or durable chokepoint control versus larger inspection/metrology competitors.
falsification_plan: Downgrade the thesis if future earnings calls or releases stop mentioning HBM, HBM4, advanced packaging, AI-driven compute, or HPC test/inspection traction.

Falsify the chokepoint thesis if the Neon HBM win remains a one-off system or engineering/evaluation tool sale without follow-on production orders over the next expected qualification and ramp cycles.

Downgrade if FY26 HPC revenue fails to approach management’s approximately $80-100 million outlook or if the revenue is mainly non-HBM legacy processor test rather than HBM/advanced-packaging inspection/metrology.
Falsify if customer count does not broaden beyond the initially disclosed leading U.S.-based memory/data-storage customer.
Downgrade if backlog, utilization, or shipment conversion weakens despite strong HBM industry demand.
Downgrade if gross margin and recurring revenue mix deteriorate, suggesting AI/HBM growth is low-margin or insufficient to change company economics.
Falsify relative-chokepoint status if competitors publicly win broader HBM4/HBM4E production inspection/metrology standards across major memory manufacturers while COHU remains niche.
Downgrade if management’s AI-driven compute TAM commentary rises but actual orders, revenue, and customer disclosures do not follow.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: The hidden signal is whether COHU’s announced HBM inspection/metrology traction converts from initial or incremental Neon platform orders into repeat production orders, multi-customer adoption, higher HBM/HPC revenue contribution, and recurring service/software/consumables economics tied to volume manufacturing.
next_research_tasks: Read the full Q1 2026 earnings-call transcript and slide deck to extract exact wording on AI-driven compute, HPC revenue, Neon, HBM, customer engagements, test-cell utilization, backlog, and design wins.

Compare Q2 2026 and Q3 2026 disclosures against the Q1 2026 outlook: track whether sales guidance converts, whether HPC revenue outlook is raised or maintained, and whether HBM inspection/metrology is named again.
Build a revenue bridge: FY2025 total revenue, 2025 HBM forecasted revenue, FY26 HPC revenue outlook, and estimated legacy semi-test revenue to quantify how material the AI/HBM angle can become.
Search for customer-side validation from memory makers, OSATs, or advanced-packaging manufacturers that use Neon/Krypton or COHU inspection/metrology tools in HBM workflows.

Map competitors in HBM inspection/metrology and back-end test, including larger process-control and semi-cap vendors, then compare throughput, accuracy, automation integration, and line-of-record evidence.
Check whether COHU’s recurring revenue claim is tied to HBM growth through service, spares, contactors, interface products, software analytics, or whether it is mostly legacy installed-base support.
Monitor 10-Q risk factors and customer concentration disclosures for evidence that AI/HBM growth is concentrated or diversifying.

Track sell-side and investor-presentation language changes: upgrade thesis only if HBM/advanced-packaging moves from narrative to quantified revenue, backlog, customer count, or production deployment metrics.

Interview or source industry-channel checks with memory packaging/test engineers, OSAT procurement, or inspection/metrology specialists to determine whether Neon is considered a production-critical tool or a niche supplementary station.

Create a falsification dashboard with quarterly fields: HBM orders, repeat orders, customer count, HPC revenue, HBM revenue, backlog, test-cell utilization, gross margin, recurring revenue percentage, and management mentions.
risks: Single-customer or narrow-customer risk: the disclosed HBM orders may remain concentrated with one memory/data-storage customer rather than becoming an industry-standard production workflow.

Scale risk: HBM revenue of $10-11 million forecasted for 2025 is evidence of traction but still small relative to total company revenue; the thesis needs confirmation that FY26 HPC revenue reaches or exceeds the $80-100 million outlook and carries attractive margins.
Cycle risk: COHU remains exposed to broader semiconductor test cycles, automotive, mobile, industrial, and other legacy end markets; weakness there could offset AI/HBM growth.
Competitive risk: larger process-control, inspection, metrology, and test-equipment vendors may win broader HBM and advanced-packaging production slots.
Qualification risk: an evaluation or early production win may not translate into repeat line-of-record orders if throughput, accuracy, uptime, integration, or customer ROI disappoint.
Narrative risk: investors may over-map COHU to AI/HBM before revenue mix, backlog, and customer count prove the link.

Margin/mix risk: HBM-related systems may not produce the same recurring revenue profile as service, consumables, interface products, or analytics; gross margin and operating leverage must be monitored.
Disclosure risk: management may provide directional commentary without enough granularity to isolate HBM inspection/metrology revenue from broader high-performance-compute test revenue.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: AI infrastructure demand → AI accelerators / ASICs / GPUs → HBM memory stacks and advanced packaging → wafer/package-level assembly, inspection, metrology, back-end test, automation, interface products, software analytics → production yield, sorting, qualification, and utilization monitoring. COHU sits one to two steps upstream from visible AI servers: not in GPU design or data-center racks, but in the manufacturing quality-control layer for devices such as HBM and high-performance processors.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 假设：HBM4、AI 加速器与先进封装提高了器件复杂度、微凸点数量、外观缺陷控制和量产良率要求，进而增加后道 inspection、metrology、test automation 与数据分析需求。COHU 已披露 Neon 平台获得 HBM inspection/metrology 追加订单，并在 2026 年一季度提高 AI-driven compute 可服务市场和 FY26 HPC 收入展望；如果这些订单从单一客户或初期平台销售演变为多客户复购、量产线部署、服务/软件/耗材附着和可见收入占比提升，则 COHU 可能从传统半导体周期复苏标的，被重新理解为 AI memory / advanced-packaging yield-control 链条上的小型卡点。当前证据等级：事实支持“有 HBM 订单和管理层持续披露”；推论支持“AI/HBM 复杂度提高可能增加 inspection/metrology 需求”；核心 chokepoint 结论仍为 hypothesis。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Hypothesis: HBM4, AI accelerators, and advanced packaging increase device complexity, micro-pillar density, cosmetic/structural defect sensitivity, and production-yield requirements, which can raise demand for back-end inspection, metrology, test automation, and analytics. Cohu has disclosed additional Neon platform orders for HBM inspection/metrology and raised its AI-driven compute TAM and FY26 HPC revenue outlook in Q1 2026. If these orders become repeat production deployments, broaden beyond one customer, and create meaningful revenue plus service/software attachment, COHU could be reframed from a cyclical back-end semiconductor test supplier into a small but relevant AI memory / advanced-packaging yield-control chokepoint. Current evidence quality: facts support the existence of HBM orders and recurring company commentary; inference supports rising inspection/metrology demand; the chokepoint conclusion remains a hypothesis.
deep_reports.title_cn: COHU：从周期性后道测试设备商，到 HBM 良率控制小卡点的待验证路径
deep_reports.title_en: COHU: A Potential HBM Yield-Control Chokepoint Hidden Inside Back-End Semiconductor Test
deep_reports.why_underfollowed: COHU is usually screened and labeled as a cyclical back-end semiconductor test equipment supplier, so generalist investors may group it with broad semi-cap recovery rather than AI infrastructure bottlenecks. The AI signal is indirect: it appears in inspection/metrology, HBM production qualification, test-cell utilization, and high-performance-compute revenue outlook rather than in headline GPU, server, networking, or data-center capex categories. This creates a potential attention gap, but also a thesis-quality risk because the AI exposure must be proven through orders, revenue mix, and customer breadth rather than narrative association.

summary: Split Layer 5 deep reports generated one target at a time.
